text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Vietnam and Austria should have more exchanges of senior delegations and experts to further cooperation between the two countries, National Assembly Chairman Nong Duc Manh said.

-- According to a new draft on foreign credit prepared by the State Bank of Vietnam, business enteprises are now allowed to take credit from foreign sources in the form of cash, merchandise, bonds, bills issued by enteprises, loans and credit.
-- The Court of Appeal in Ho Chi Minh City is scheduled on Monday to annouce verdicts in Tamexco case, defendants of which were charged with causing losses of about $50 million.
-- Two state-owned companies in Ho Chi Minh City have applied to sell shares to foreign investors, an official from the City Equitisation Steering Board said.
-- Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh visited Vietnam for the first time as premier to enhance economic relations and discuss maritime boudaries and fishing rights.
-- The Vietnamese national football team's coach, Karl Heinz Weigang, resigned from this post and left Ho Chi Minh City for Malaysia on Sunday.
